title: Step Supporting Validator Unit Association Contract

scope.purpose: Define the architectural relationship between a concrete Step Supporting Validator Unit instance and the Step-defined processing scope or scopes for which that validator unit is applicable.
scope.appliesTo: A concrete Step specialization that selects one or more Step Supporting Validator Unit instances.

stepSupportingValidatorUnit.meaning: A validator component selected by a concrete Step as an optional supporting pattern for validation responsibilities required by that Step.
stepSupportingValidatorUnit.classification: A Step Supporting Pattern with its own specialized behavioral contract; it is not an instance of a universal SupportingUnit base type.

association.meaning: An explicit, identity-bearing relationship that makes a particular validator-unit instance applicable to a particular Step-owned validation scope under the concrete Step's specialization.

associationTarget.meaning: The Step-owned processing scope to which a validator-unit instance is assigned for applicability.
permittedScopeKinds: A concrete SPU instance within the owning Step.
The owning Step instance as a whole.
Another explicitly identified internal processing scope defined by the concrete Step.

optionality: A Step is not required to select or associate any Step Supporting Validator Unit.
The existence of this contract does not make validation mandatory for every Step.
A concrete Step selects validator units only when its processing responsibility requires validation.
scopeFlexibility: A validator-unit association is not restricted to one SPU.
A validator-unit instance may be associated with a Step-level scope, an SPU-level scope, or another Step-defined internal processing scope.
The concrete Step defines the permitted target scopes for each validator-unit instance and association.
specialization: This contract defines reusable association semantics and constraints, not a universal association topology.
The concrete Step specializes target scope, cardinality, multiplicity, exclusivity, validity, and change rules.
No universal one-validator-per-SPU, one-SPU-per-validator, or one-validator-per-Step relationship is imposed.
compositionAuthority: The owning Step Composition is authoritative for establishing, admitting, coordinating, changing, and ending validator-unit associations within the Step's internal composition.
Association with a particular SPU does not transfer association-management authority to that SPU.
The SPU remains responsible only for its own processing contract and any explicitly assigned interaction with the validator.

validatorUnit.description: Identifies the concrete validator-unit instance participating in the association.

target.description: Identifies the Step-owned target scope to which the validator-unit instance is associated.

association.description: Identifies this particular relationship independently of the identities of its participants.

owningStep.description: Establishes the Step boundary within which the association is valid.

identityRequirements: The association must be distinguishable from both the validator-unit instance and its target scope.
The association identity must be unique within the identity scope defined by the concrete Step for as long as the association or any retained result/reference to it may be observed.
The association identity remains stable for the lifetime of that association.
Ending an association and later establishing a logically similar association creates a new association identity when prior association evidence may still be observed.
The target identity must identify both the target scope kind and the concrete target instance; an SPU identity alone must not be interpreted as a Step-level target.
The concrete Step defines identity representations and generation mechanisms. No UUID, counter, address, timestamp, or other specific mechanism is mandated.

validatorUnitIdentity identifies one concrete validator-unit instance within the identity scope defined by the concrete Step; it is independent of every association in which that instance participates.

Each distinct relationship between that validator-unit instance and one target scope has its own validatorUnitAssociationIdentity. Therefore, one validator-unit instance associated with three distinct target scopes is represented by one validatorUnitIdentity and three distinct association identities.
Adding, ending, or replacing an association does not create a new validator-unit identity unless the validator-unit instance itself is replaced.
A validator-unit instance identity must not be derived from, or overloaded to represent, an association target or association identity.

An association identity identifies exactly one validator-unit instance-to-target relationship within one owning Step instance; it is not a reusable identifier for a relationship to a different target.
scopeBinding: Every association belongs to exactly one owning Step instance.
Every association identifies exactly one association target scope.
A validator-unit instance may participate in multiple associations only when the concrete Step specialization permits that multiplicity.
An association target may have multiple validator-unit associations only when the concrete Step specialization permits that multiplicity.
An association must not refer to a target outside the owning Step's internal composition.

cardinalityAndMultiplicity.commonContractRule: This contract imposes no universal cardinality or multiplicity beyond the identity and single-target requirements of each individual association.
specializationObligations: The concrete Step defines the allowed number of validator-unit instances associated with each target scope.
The concrete Step defines whether one validator-unit instance may serve multiple target scopes.
The concrete Step defines whether multiple validator-unit instances may serve the same target scope.
The concrete Step defines whether associations are exclusive, shared, or conditionally shared.
The concrete Step defines any constraints that depend on validator role, validation responsibility, invocation mode, or concurrency.

associationIdentitySemantics.relationshipIdentity: validatorUnitAssociationIdentity identifies one relationship instance, not the validator-unit instance and not the target scope.

multiTargetExample.validatorUnitInstance: One validator-unit instance identified by validatorUnitIdentity.
multiTargetExample.targetScopes: Three distinct target scopes identified independently.
multiTargetExample.requiredAssociations: Three association records, each with a distinct validatorUnitAssociationIdentity and the same validatorUnitIdentity, each bound to exactly one target identity.

identityIndependence: The validator-unit instance may participate in multiple associations when the concrete Step specialization permits it.
Each association remains independently identifiable and independently terminable.
Ending one association does not end another association involving the same validator-unit instance.
Ending all associations does not, by itself, release or dispose the validator-unit instance.

StepComposition: Select the validator-unit instances admitted into the Step's internal composition according to the concrete Step design.
Establish and maintain the association between each selected validator-unit instance and its Step-defined target scope.
Validate that the target scope belongs to the owning Step and is permitted by the concrete Step specialization.
Assign or obtain the association identity according to the Step's identity rules.
Coordinate association changes and dissociation without invalidating active invocations or retained evidence.
Make the applicable validator-unit associations available to the Step-specific invocation and flow coordination.
Remain the sole authority responsible for creating, changing, rebinding, and ending associations within the Step; any component request for such a change is resolved and enacted by Step Composition.
Maintain the authoritative association state and the association-to-participant identity mapping for the period required by active use and retained evidence.
StepSupportingValidatorUnit: Expose or satisfy the association-related identity and applicability requirements defined by its specialized contract.
Operate only within the target scope and authorized context supplied by the owning Step composition.
Retain its own validation semantics and result contract; association does not transfer those responsibilities to Step Composition.
Must not independently create, change, rebind, or end an association, or alter its target or association identity.
May report that an association appears unusable or request an association change through the owning Step Composition; such a report or request does not itself change association state.
SPU: May be the target of a validator-unit association.
Does not acquire ownership of the validator-unit instance merely because the association targets that SPU.
Does not acquire authority to select, create, change, rebind, or end the association, nor to alter its association identity or target binding.
May consume the association context or validator result made available under the concrete Step's interaction design, and may report a need for change to Step Composition.
Any SPU-originated request concerning an association is advisory; Step Composition alone decides whether and how the association is changed.
StageComposition: Does not select, establish, mutate, or manage associations among a Step's internal validator units and target scopes.
Pipeline: Does not impose a global validator-unit association registry, manager, or association topology.

validityConditions: The owning Step instance is identifiable and active under its own lifecycle contract.
The validator-unit instance is admitted into the owning Step's internal composition.
The target scope is identifiable, belongs to the owning Step, and is permitted by the concrete Step specialization.
The association identity is valid and does not collide within its required observation scope.
The association satisfies the concrete Step's cardinality, multiplicity, exclusivity, and compatibility constraints.
invalidationConditions: The association is explicitly ended under the concrete Step's dissociation rules.
The validator-unit instance is no longer admitted for use by the owning Step.
The target scope ceases to exist or ceases to be a permitted target under the concrete Step's rules.
A concrete Step-defined condition makes the association invalid, provided active invocations and retained evidence are handled according to the specialization.
associationValidity.validationResponsibility: Step Composition validates and enforces association validity when establishing or changing associations. The concrete Step defines any additional semantic compatibility checks.

changeRules: The common contract does not require associations to be mutable after establishment.
The concrete Step defines whether an association may be changed during the lifetime of the Step instance.
The concrete Step defines whether association changes are prohibited during an active validator invocation, an active target invocation, or another protected processing interval.

A change that alters the target or validator participant is treated as ending the previous association and establishing a new association unless the concrete Step explicitly defines a safe in-place modification with preserved identity semantics.
Association changes must not silently redirect an already-started invocation or rewrite the association identity recorded in previously retained evidence.
dissociationRules: Dissociation is decided, coordinated, and recorded by Step Composition.
Step Composition establishes the effective end point of the association. From that point onward, no new validator invocation may rely on that association.
The concrete Step defines how active invocations are completed, cancelled, or otherwise reconciled before dissociation is considered complete.
Dissociation does not itself dispose, destroy, or release the validator-unit instance; those actions belong to the applicable Lifecycle Contract and Step lifecycle policy.
Dissociation does not erase validation results, invocation evidence, or provenance already produced under the association.

Any retained result or evidence that requires association provenance must preserve sufficient identity information to identify the validator-unit instance, the ended association, its target scope, and the relevant validator invocation, as applicable to the concrete result contract.

The association identity and the minimum association descriptor needed to interpret retained references remain resolvable for the applicable evidence-retention period; this may be achieved through retained identity metadata and does not require retaining the validator-unit runtime instance.
Retention of association identity metadata or validation results must not, by itself, extend the validator-unit instance lifetime, prevent its release, or require the instance to remain callable.
The concrete Step defines evidence/result retention and release conditions independently from validator-unit instance lifecycle and resource release.
Ending one association does not affect other active associations of the same validator-unit instance.
Dissociation does not rewrite or reassign the provenance of results produced before its effective end point.

postDissociationEvidence.principle: Historical association provenance must remain interpretable without retaining the validator-unit runtime instance solely for that purpose.
requiredDistinction: Association validity for future invocation ends at the association's effective end point.
Historical identity/provenance may remain referable for as long as retained results or evidence require it.
Validator-unit runtime lifetime and association-evidence retention are separate concerns.
minimumRetainedProvenance: validatorInvocationIdentity where defined by the behavioral contract
postDissociationEvidence.retentionAuthority: The concrete Step defines the retention period and storage/representation of result and evidence content. This Association Contract requires provenance continuity but does not prescribe a storage mechanism or a universal retention duration.

invocationAndResultBoundary.principle: Association establishes applicability only. It does not define when, how, or how often a validator unit is invoked, nor how its result is interpreted.
rules: Step Composition determines invocation timing and coordination according to the concrete Step's flow design and the validator-unit behavioral contract.
The association identity and target identity should be available to invocation evidence whenever required to correlate a validation result with the scope for which it was produced.
The validator unit retains ownership of validation semantics and its specialized result meaning.
The concrete Step defines whether and how a validator result contributes to Step-specific flow decisions or StepValidatorResult.
Association does not imply that validation must occur before, after, or concurrently with SPU processing.
Association does not imply that a validation failure terminates the Step or prevents another component from being invoked.

A validator invocation is correlated with the specific association under which it was authorized; the validator-unit identity alone is insufficient to identify which target association applied when one instance participates in multiple associations.
A result produced under an association retains that association's identity as historical provenance even after the association ends.

The association identity is not a substitute for a validator invocation identity; repeated invocations under the same association remain distinguishable by invocation identity where the behavioral contract requires it.

lifecycleBoundary.principle: This contract defines association establishment and termination, not the lifecycle of the validator-unit instance.
rules: Provisioning, initialization, readiness, reuse, retention, and release of validator-unit instances are governed by Step_Supporting_Validator_Unit_Lifecycle_Contract.json.
Association establishment may require an already provisioned or admitted validator-unit instance, but this contract does not prescribe the provisioning sequence.
Ending an association is not equivalent to releasing the validator-unit instance.
The concrete Step and its Step Composition coordinate association and lifecycle decisions without assuming that association lifetime and instance lifetime are identical.
The end of an association does not imply that the validator-unit instance has reached the end of its lifecycle; the same instance may remain admitted and participate in other valid associations.

Retention of historical association metadata or validation-result provenance must not be implemented by retaining the validator-unit instance unless the separate Lifecycle Contract independently requires that instance to remain alive.
Step Composition coordinates the association end and separately applies the Lifecycle Contract's instance-retention and release rules.

explicitNonGoals: No universal SupportingUnit base type or shared runtime interface is introduced.
No mandatory validator unit is imposed on any Step.
No universal association topology, cardinality, multiplicity, or exclusivity is imposed.
No association with Stage, Pipeline, or an external owner is introduced by this contract.
No validator execution signature, validation algorithm, validation status taxonomy, or result schema is defined here.
No invocation ordering, scheduling, retry, concurrency, or flow-control policy is defined here.
No validator-unit provisioning, initialization, readiness, reuse, disposal, or resource-ownership protocol is defined here.
No global registry, central manager, service locator, or mediator is required.
No language-specific class hierarchy, pointer model, serialization format, or storage representation is mandated.
No rule requires a validator-unit instance to be retained merely because an ended association is still referenced by historical evidence.
No SPU is granted association-management authority merely because it is the association target.
No association identity is reused to represent multiple target relationships.
specializationRequirements: Identify the concrete Step scope or scopes to which validator units may be associated.
Define the target scope kinds permitted for each validator-unit role.
Define validator-unit identity and target-scope identity representations and uniqueness scopes.
Define association identity representation, assignment authority, and observation lifetime.
Define cardinality, multiplicity, sharing, and exclusivity rules.
Define semantic compatibility checks between each validator-unit role and its target scope.
Define whether associations are immutable or mutable and the protected intervals during which changes are prohibited.
Define dissociation behavior when active invocations or retained validation evidence exist.
Define the correlation information retained with validator invocation evidence and results.
Define whether one validator-unit instance may participate in multiple simultaneous associations and the applicable concurrency constraints.
Define the effective end-point and reconciliation policy for dissociation while validator or target invocations are active.
Define the minimum association provenance retained with each validation result/evidence item and its retention period independently from validator-unit instance lifetime.
Define how ended association identities and their minimal descriptors remain resolvable without requiring retention of the validator-unit runtime instance.
Define the permitted SPU interactions with an association, explicitly excluding independent association creation, mutation, rebinding, or termination.

references.relationship: Step Composition authority for internal component composition, association coordination, and invocation flow.
Step Aggregate Root boundary and public Step-facing contract.
SPU identity, processing responsibility, and boundary when an SPU is an association target.
SPU-scoped validator-result integration and invocation evidence.
Validator-unit instance lifecycle, reuse, retention, and release contract.
Framework-level association coordination invariants refined by this specialized Association Contract; specialized identity names and behavior remain authoritative.

openDesignDetails: Define the concrete validator-unit identity and invocation-correlation fields in the validator behavioral contract.
Define the exact Step-level and SPU-level validator result representations in their respective result contracts.
Define whether one validator-unit instance can be shared across multiple concurrent target invocations and the guarantees required for such sharing.
Define the concrete Step's evidence-retention period and the minimal historical association descriptor required to interpret retained validator results.

frameworkCoordination.conformance: This contract specializes the shared Step Composition coordination invariants. Where the shared contract defines only conceptual identity roles or lifecycle distinctions, this document supplies the component-specific identity names, semantics, mechanics, and constraints.
frameworkCoordination.precedence: The common contract governs cross-cutting Step Composition coordination invariants. This specialized contract governs component-specific behavior and mechanics. Neither contract changes the component pattern?s distinct behavioral result semantics.

frameworkIdentityRoleMapping.targetIdentitySemantics: associationTargetIdentity identifies both the target scope kind and the concrete target instance within the owning Step; it must not be represented by a bare SPU identity when the target scope may instead be Step-wide or another Step-internal scope.
